predicted: Re-runs the three pools that started before the honest-ceiling columns existed, so all eleven carry the same columns. The shared columns were verified purely additive on a 1-seed lendingclub probe: 34 of 34 bit-identical, three added. WHY: oracle_lambda chooses lambda on the very rows it is scored on, so the gap between it and a deployable policy is part optimism and part recoverable selection loss, and section 6 cannot currently say which. The first RB pool made this live -- 3-fold CV recovered only 3.6% of the gap, which is either a weak selector or a ceiling that was never there. oracle_half, oracle_honest and blend_half measure all three legs at the SAME sample size (half of test), so their differences are optimism and headroom rather than sample-size artefacts. PREDICTION: the honest headroom (oracle_honest - blend_half) is a SMALL fraction of the apparent gap (oracle_half - blend_half). A 1-seed lendingclub probe gave 10.7%. READ THAT PRECISELY: the honest headroom is what an HONEST SELECTOR OF COMPARABLE SIZE achieves over the deployable one, with no optimism in either. Note the sizes, which are easy to get backwards: val is 30% of 70% = 21% of the target's rows and |te|/2 is 15%, so oracle_honest selects on FEWER rows than blend already uses. A near-zero honest headroom therefore does NOT show that more selection data would fail to help -- blend_cv, which uses 3-fold CV over the whole training set, beats blend on every pool measured so far. What oracle_half against oracle_honest isolates is OPTIMISM at a fixed sample size. The apparent gap uses oracle_half, which picks lambda on half the rows and therefore overfits MORE than oracle_lambda does on the full test set. The ratio is therefore directional evidence that better selection cannot close the published gap; it is NOT an estimate of how inflated oracle_lambda is, and that sentence must not be written. If it holds across the eleven pools, section 6 should report honest headroom alongside the oracle share and treat oracle_lambda as a bound on interpolation policies rather than as attainable. WITHDRAWAL: if the honest headroom exceeds half the apparent gap, better selection can close much of the gap, the selection-loss reading stands, and this diagnostic is a negative control rather than a correction.
